methods.name: Stage-Progression

methods.name: Peer-Median

methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
XMOS is a Growth-stage semiconductor company that has raised £200M+ to date. The valuation landscape includes 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers in Chips & Semiconductors, though no narrow-filter peer set of sufficient size exists for conventional multiples-based triangulation.

Stage-Progression methodology is applicable and forms the primary anchor. Using total raised (£200M) as a proxy for recent valuation, a standard 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for Growth-to-next-stage progression yields £240M. This method is the only triangulation approach supported by available data; Peer-Median analysis fails due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum thresholds (0 of 3+ required), and Public-Comp Anchoring cannot be applied absent XMOS's revenue disclosure.

The triangulated valuation range is £204M (low) to £276M (median at £240M, high at £276M), reflecting ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression result. This range should be treated with appropriate caution given reliance on a single method and the absence of revenue data to cross-check against public semiconductor multiples (median 18.4x P/S). Key uncertainties include the stability of the £200M+ raised figure as a valuation proxy, XMOS's revenue and growth trajectory relative to the identified private peer set (Cerebras, SambaNova, Etched, Ayar Labs), and whether next-stage funding has materially reset valuations.
